question: within the shared builtin->bytecode callback bridge tax, is there one stage hit on every callback that explains >=40% (~11 cycles/callback) and is isolable by a single-mechanism change

binaries.note: both cold-cache builds of 0e4ee496 produced the identical binary, so this tree contributes no build bistability; the noise ruler is two independent full timing sweeps (T1, T2) on the same binary

comment: P7-42 stage table. Stage names come from the ACTUAL chain read out of the
shipped binary's DWARF line table, not from an a-priori list.
Every range is a file:line window in this worktree at 0e4ee496, and every
stage is SYMBOL-SCOPED: shared inline helpers (Vm.next, byteCode(),
loadCurrentLevel, Stack.topPtr, JSValue.dup) occur in more than one of the
mapped symbols, so an unscoped file:line table leaks samples between the
driver-re-entry stage and the callback's own return handler.
S* = on the builtin->bytecode callback bridge.
C* = present on the direct-control path as well.
X* = legs this corpus never takes; their sample counts are the instrument's

popAndResume (tailcall_dispatch.zig:1069-1204) is inlined into BOTH op_return and op_return_undef; forEach's noop callback retires through op_return_undef while some/every/filter's predicate callbacks retire through op_return, so both symbols must be mapped or three of the four families lose their whole return column.

S7 is split into five sub-stages so the report can separate work that is re-derived from state the push path already held (S7c/S7d) from the cost of the driver activation itself (S7b) and from the dispatch entry (S7e). The split is by file:line within the same three symbols; the sum of the five equals the single S7 bucket of the earlier run.

stages.name: S1_callsite_entry_and_poll
stages.what: noinline call-site prologue, one interrupt poll, active-invocation identity check, native-boundary-simple eligibility test

stages.name: S2_fence_scope_construct
stages.what: NativeBoundaryScope.init: capture the outer view, runtime pointer, MachineBacktraceView.segment over the current top, fence_depth snapshot

stages.name: S3_fence_publish
stages.what: NativeBoundaryScope.push: freeze the outer backtrace view, build the ActiveBacktraceFrame, link it into rt.hot.current_backtrace_frame, repoint invocation.current_backtrace_view

stages.name: S4_frame_admission
stages.what: planned stack bytes, runtime depth/byte budget commit, Entry slot lookup, VM stack arena carve

stages.name: S5_argument_staging
stages.what: carve the arg_count-wide parameter window, duplicate min(3, arity) callback arguments into it, clear the tail

stages.name: S6_entry_publication
stages.what: write the callback Entry: return_action=.native_boundary, catch target, profile guard, arena mark, complete Frame record, Stack arena window, teardown bits, prev link, depth bump

stages.name: S8_special_return
stages.what: return-handler special-return test, native-boundary arm, popReturnedNativeBoundary teardown, publish vm.return_value and the .native_returned outcome; op_return reaches the same arm through popAndResume's action switch

stages.name: S9_fence_restore
stages.what: NativeBoundaryScope.finish: unlink the ActiveBacktraceFrame, restore invocation.current_backtrace_view, re-liven the outer view

stages.name: S10_return_to_builtin
stages.what: hand the callback result back out of the noinline call site and restore the builtin's own register state

stages.name: X11a_fallback_args_hoisted
stages.what: argument loads for the never-taken authoritative fallback call, hoisted by the compiler into the unconditional prologue

stages.name: X11b_fallback_call_cold
stages.what: NOT TAKEN: the authoritative JS_Call-shaped fallback call itself

stages.name: X11c_owned_copy_leg
stages.what: NOT TAKEN: OwnedArgList leg for non-simple-eligible callees

stages.name: C90_leaf_return_arms
stages.what: shared with the direct control: op_return_undef zero-arg / exact-args leaf return arms and their inline epilogues

stages.name: S7a_fence_depth_check_and_driver_call
stages.what: runActiveInvocationUntilNativeBoundary: fence-depth check, the call into the driver, and the post-return depth/top asserts

stages.name: S7b_driver_frame_save_restore
stages.what: the runTC activation itself: callee-saved register save/restore for a frame that has the whole inlined run() live-range

stages.name: S7c_vm_cache_rebuild
stages.what: rebuild the Vm cache: Machine.loadCurrentLevel (depth branch, machine.top, &entry.frame/&entry.stack/&entry.catch_target), frame.function, function.byteCode(), then ten Vm field stores

stages.name: S7d_run_prologue
stages.what: run(): dispatch-table pointers, local_fast_blocked re-derivation, pc = code_base + frame.pc, sp = stack.topPtr(), var_buf = frame.locals.ptr

stages.name: S7e_dispatch_entry_and_outcome
stages.what: the call into next() and the run-loop outcome switch that turns .native_returned into the driver's return value

why_not_a_single_mechanism: S7b is the ABI cost of a separate driver activation whose live range spans the whole inlined run(); removing it means relocating the interpreter loop relative to the native boundary, not deleting work.
S7c is 31 instructions of which roughly two thirds are the ten Vm field stores that any driver entry must perform; only the re-derivation loads are redundant.
S7d is run()'s prologue, shared verbatim with every other driver entry in the engine (script entry, generator resume, constructor completion), so changing it changes non-bridge paths.
S7a carries the fence-depth-bounded error contract (runActiveInvocationAfterNativeBoundaryError); it is not derived state.
S7e is the dispatch entry plus the outcome switch; the direct bytecode call pays an equivalent dispatch, so this is bridge-specific placement rather than bridge-specific work.

instrument_zero_check.interpretation: a 19-instruction block that provably never executes still collects 0.86 cyc and 6.6 insn per callback, so per-stage attribution carries roughly +-1 cycle of leakage; every reported stage except S3_fence_publish sits well above that floor, and no stage comes near 11 cycles
instrument_zero_check.opposite_direction_check: C90_leaf_return_arms has gdb 1.0000 hits/callback in the direct control and 0.0000 in the builtin; sampling reads 3.94 cyc in the control and 0.43 in the builtin, so the instrument tracks presence in both directions

aliasing_hazard.description: the first record pass used perf -F 49999 (auto-tuned period). On this workload the inner period is ~100 cycles and the tuned period locked near a multiple of it: in the -F record of q_every a single `bl next` return site took 20.09% of all process cycles, against 0.74% at the same instruction in the -F record of q_foreach, and the S7 bucket read 43.99 cyc/callback instead of 21.8. All reported numbers come from fixed, mutually co-prime periods (cycles 50021/65599/82657, instructions 249989/300007/350003, stalls 24011/30011/36011) and the min/max across periods is carried in the per-family records.

decision.text:
Decision:
    shared bridge tax confirmed,
    but distributed across required control state;
    no one-cut.

not_established: no per-stage ledger: the cycle column is sampled attribution, and on an out-of-order core a backend stall is charged to the consumer at the end of a dependency chain rather than to the instruction that created it. The per-stage cycles must not be summed into an exact 27-cycle account, and they are not: the bridge stages sum to 58.5 cyc/callback while the net tax is 27.3, because the builtin path also does not pay the 28.5-29.1 cyc/element bytecode loop scaffold.
no measurement of how many cycles any candidate change would actually recover: no src/ change was built or timed.
the split of S7c into 'mandatory Vm stores' versus 'redundant re-derivation loads' is a static reading of the disassembly, not a measured split.

S1_callsite_entry_and_poll is reported as a bridge stage because it is 0 in the direct control's mapped symbols, but the direct bytecode call path also polls interrupts inside its own op_call handler; the poll itself is therefore not bridge-specific and S1's 2.75 cyc overstates the bridge-only part of that stage.
only the four no-result-write dense Array builtins were measured. map, filter(true), reduce, find*, TypedArray callbacks, sparse/holey receivers and cross-realm callbacks were not.

the callback-arity sweep isolates the argument-window mechanism on the builtin side only; its mirrored controls at arity 0/1/2 pass three actuals into a narrower callee and take the bytecode padded-argc path, so the control side of that sweep is not a clean baseline and is reported but not used as a rung.
S5's dup loop is the one stage whose dynamic hit count is not 1 per callback (4.0000/callback at inline_calls.zig:3456: loop header plus three iterations); every other bridge stage is exactly 1.0000.
ARM SPE is present on this host but was not used; all attribution rests on non-precise PMU sampling with the leakage floor quantified above.
no claim that the fence, the Machine save, special_return, argument ownership or native-caller state is redundant. Each was measured, none was shown removable.
